pairs.subject: migrations
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/db/core.ts:317 The database boot sequence runs schema mutations and table rebuilds directly on startup without a pre-migration snapshot gate, version ledger bump, or rollback halt policy.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/db/add-columns.ts:58 Guarded column addition operates without an authoritative version ledger, re-evaluating schema existence on every boot.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:317 ensureDb opens the connection and mutates the schema on boot without taking an automated pre-migration snapshot.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:2881 rebuildTable transactions lack dependent object re-creation and omit foreign key verification prior to commit.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:1859 migrateUniqueIndex catches unique constraint failures and returns instead of halting the migration chain.
app/_lib/db/core-migrations.test.ts:211 The migration upgrade test uses a synthetic inline database rather than an authentic checked-in fixture from the oldest release.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:3785 The data backfill skips invalid records without performing count reconciliation with predicates to loudly fail the step.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:30 The application runs against an isolated local SQLite file singleton per process with no concurrent rolling deployments.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:321 The database schema consists of fixed static application tables declared in code with no operator-defined dynamic table sets.
app/_lib/db/core.ts:4 SQLite provides transactional storage capable of atomic metadata recording, making data-shape derivation inapplicable.

pairs.registryProposal: The migrations standard treats ledger-less replay as a recognized variant in the golden path overview, but the idempotent-steps technique mandates 'Ledger always'; the standard should align these sections to clearly specify acceptable invariants for ledger-less embedded engines.
